text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Committee of Privileges quizzes secretary-general of Singapore Democratic Party for seven hours regarding accusations of perjury, prevarication, misconduct and wilfully giving false evidence.
- EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan says labour conditions and investment are two problems for World Trade Organisation agenda.
- Jurong Town Corporation will spend Singapore $2.2 billion on industrial development plan for land and factories.
- Listed United Pulp & Paper Company Ltd joins forces with European paper manufacturer to explore setting up of plants in Asia.
- Singapore-China Suzhou Industrial Park granted special duty-free import quotas to allow overseas investors to import capital goods free of duty until 2000.
- Shipowner Osprey Maritime keen to convert US dollar shares listed on stock exchange into Singapore dollars.
- CityCab, a venture between Singapore Bus Service and ST Automotive, will probably launch premier service of Mercedes cabs by December.
- Hasan and Sampoerna strike deal on Astra's future shareholding patterns.
- Garment maker and retailer Heshe Holdings is raising Singapore $11.1 million through private placement of 28 million 25-cent shares at 40 cents each.
- Singapore Finance Minister Richard Hu urges Chinese companies and financial institutions to use Singapore as base to raise funds.
- Malaysia Mining Corporation Bhd expects profit lower than Malaysian $121 million forecast.
